item.title: Marketing Operations Manager (fixed term) at SafetyWing
item.description:
🧘 Benefits beyond base pay:

  • Fully remote work environment – work from anywhere globally
  • Our own global safety net, giving you worldwide health, income, and travel coverage
  • Potential to unlock equity compensation, yearly home office allowance and more!

🚀 We look forward to hearing from you!
At SafetyWing (YC W18), we’re building a global social safety net for remote workers—simple health, insurance, and retirement products designed to replace national welfare systems. Our mission is to remove geographical borders as a barrier to equal opportunity and freedom for everyone. If we succeed, we believe this will be one of the most important tasks of our time.

🌎 About this Role

We're looking for a Marketing Operations Manager on a fixed-term contract of 6-12 months, covering a team member's planned leave. You'll keep a busy marketing department organized and moving. That means tracking projects across the team, running the regular team meetings, making sure decisions turn into action, and keeping leadership informed.

This is an operations and project management role for someone with real marketing know-how. You won't set strategy or run channels. You will need to understand how campaigns, launches, webinars and events come together, so you can spot what's missing, what's late and what needs a decision.

You'll report to our Head of Marketing and work closely with campaign, content, creative, events, lifecycle and sales colleagues across our consumer and B2B businesses.

💻 What you'll do

Keep the department's work moving
  • Keep a clear view of projects running at the same time across the team: their deadlines, dependencies and risks.
  • Run the department's recurring meetings, write down decisions and make sure actions get done.
  • Follow up with contributors and clear routine blockers yourself. When a decision is needed, bring leadership clear options.
  • Send leadership short, regular updates on progress, risks and what needs attention.
Help campaigns and launches come together
  • Help campaign leads turn priorities into plans with clear owners, timelines, deliverables and launch dates.
  • Coordinate the moving parts across copy, design, web, email, events and Sales follow-up so launches land on time.
  • Check that each launch is ready: assets, follow-up journey, Sales handoff and basic tracking, as agreed with the campaign lead.
  • Spot gaps early and raise them, such as a campaign with no follow-up or a launch nobody owns.
Keep the basics in good shape
  • Keep the team's processes practical and repeatable. Improve them where it helps, without adding admin.
  • Keep our project management setup current and well used.
  • Pull together routine updates from existing reports and dashboards when leadership needs them.
Hand back cleanly
  • Learn how the department runs from the current Marketing Operations Manager before their leave, and take over agreed responsibilities step by step.
  • Document what you run so the hand back is smooth. Keep a short record of what changed and what's still open.

🧪 What we're looking for

  • Around 4 or more years in marketing operations, marketing project management, program management or a similar role inside a marketing team
  • A strong record of keeping many projects moving at once, with people who don't report to you
  • Enough marketing experience to understand how campaigns, launches, webinars, events and Sales handoffs work, and to tell when something isn't ready
  • Comfort with project management tools, a CRM and marketing automation. HubSpot experience is a plus
  • Clear, proactive written communication on a remote team, and sound prioritization. You know when to handle something yourself and when to escalate
  • Able to start immediately, and comfortable joining a team mid-stride for a defined period

😀 We like to work with people who:
  • Want to help build a global social safety net on the Internet.
  • Think for themselves instead of copying others.
  • Are willing to try new things, even with the risk of failure.
  • Are intellectually curious and open to new ideas.
  • Are creative and bold in the face of any problems.
  • Have strong integrity and do the right thing.

item.title: Technical Enablement Engineer at LiveKit
item.description:
About LiveKit

LiveKit is the default infrastructure layer for real-time AI — the platform that gives AI the ability to see, hear, and speak. From powering voice for millions of ChatGPT users to enabling drone teleoperation at Skydio and serving as the backbone for roughly 25% of 911 emergency calls in the U.S., LiveKit handles the real-time media layer that production AI applications depend on.

Over 300,000 developers and 5,000+ companies — from leading AI labs to Fortune 500 enterprises — run production workloads on LiveKit. We've raised $181M from investors including Index Ventures, Altimeter Capital, and Salesforce Ventures, and we're growing fast.

 

About This Role

Our product is deeply technical, and we sell into a brand-new category: voice AI infrastructure. As we grow our Sales team, our AEs, SDRs, and presales engineers need to understand how LiveKit works, and why real-time voice AI is hard, well enough to hold their own in a customer conversation.

We're hiring a Technical Enablement Engineer to own that. You'll build our technical training program from scratch, so ramp time doesn't depend on pulling engineers off the roadmap. You'll sit on the Sales team, report to our CRO, and have a direct line to the engineers building the product.

This is a hands-on, builder-first enablement role. You'll see the impact of your work directly in how fast new sellers ramp and how confident they are in front of customers.

You'll thrive here if you:

  • are known as the go-to person for tackling tough technical problems

  • can clearly explain complex technical concepts to people who aren't engineers

  • are a fast learner, frequently picking up new languages and tools

The best way to impress us is to build something with LiveKit and show us how you'd teach it to someone who has never touched it.

 

What You'll Do

  • Audit what AEs, SDRs, and presales know today and where deals stall on technical gaps

  • Build the core curriculum: LiveKit fundamentals, voice AI architecture, agents, and the competitive landscape

  • Ship hands-on labs and sandboxes so sellers build something real, not just watch slides

  • Run technical onboarding for new AEs and SDRs, and create a clear technical learning path for presales and Solutions Architects

  • Certify demo and discovery readiness through hands-on exercises

  • Keep technical content current with every product release, working directly with engineering and product

  • Measure what matters: ramp time, time to first qualified technical conversation, assessment pass rates, and seller confidence

 

Who You Are

  • A senior-level engineer or technical founder who has shipped production software

  • You've taught or enabled technical content to non-engineers (sales, SEs, or customers) and have a track record to show for it

  • You can explain complex technical concepts simply, to any audience

  • You're a fast learner who ramps quickly on new technology

 

Nice to Have

  • Ex-technical founder

  • Experience with voice AI, WebRTC, real-time systems, or LLM applications

  • Built a curriculum, bootcamp, or certification program

  • Ran SE or AE onboarding at a dev-tools or infrastructure company

 

Our Commitment to You

  • An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world

  • Competitive salary and equity package

  • Health, dental, and vision benefits

  • Flexible vacation policy

 

LiveKit is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of any characteristic protected by applicable law. If you require a reasonable accommodation during the application or interview process, please contact recruiting@example.com.

item.title: GTM, Strategic Planning at Supabase
item.description:
Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search — all deeply integrated and designed for growth. We're building the best developer platform to power the next generation of software companies, and our go-to-market team is scaling fast to match.

We're looking for a lead in Go-To-Market Strategic Planning, to shape how Supabase's GTM engine runs. This is a high-leverage, high-ownership role that sits at the intersection of strategy, data, and execution. You'll work directly with Success, Sales, Marketing, Finance, Partnerships and Product to build the systems, processes, and insights that help our go-to-market teams move faster and smarter.

What you'll do

  • Own the end-to-end GTM Strategic Planning, covering territory design, segmentation design, target planning and GTM capacity planning.

  • Build and maintain a single source of truth for planning data across HubSpot, BigQuery and Hex.

  • Translate company priorities into field actions through designing the planning strategy and seeing it through to execution.

  • Partner with Sales Leadership to design and iterate on coverage models, segmentation, and team structures that reflect how developers actually buy.

  • Define and track the metrics that matter, and surface insights that drive action, not just reporting.

  • Lead the Strategic Planning roadmap: guide and lead in tooling investments and evaluate new systems and processes against real business needs.

  • Work cross-functionally with talent acquisition, ensuring GTM and territory models stay aligned.

  • Collaborate with GTM Engineering on automations and data pipelines so that your strategy translates into working systems, not just slide decks.

We'll expect you to

  • Operate with high ownership. You set your own agenda, escalate when needed, and don't wait to be asked.

  • Work asynchronously and document clearly. We're a globally distributed team and writing is how we think.

  • Bridge strategy and execution. From drafting segmentation approaches in Google Docs to using SQL to monitor its effectiveness.

  • Build for scale without over-engineering. Simple systems that work beat perfect systems that don't ship.

  • Stay close to the customer. Developers are our buyers, and understanding how they discover, adopt, and expand is core to everything you'll do.

You might be a fit if you

  • Have 6+ years of experience in Revenue Operations, Strategy Consulting, GTM Strategy, or Sales Operations at a B2B SaaS or developer-tools company.

  • Are fluent in the GTM stack: HubSpot, BigQuery, and Hightouch.

  • Can write SQL comfortably and aren't afraid to get into the data yourself before asking an analyst.

  • Have experience designing or overhauling sales processes, forecasting cadences, or territory models in a high-growth environment.

  • Understand product-led growth motions: PLS, usage-based triggers, and how PLG data flows into commercial pipelines.

  • Thrive with autonomy and are energized by building things that didn't exist before you joined.

  • Communicate with clarity across Finance, Sales, Success, Partnerships, Engineering, and Marketing without losing nuance.

What We Offer

  • Fully Remote

    We hire globally. We believe you can do your best work from anywhere. There are no Supabase offices, but we provide a WeWork membership or co-working allowance you can use anywhere in the world.

  • ESOP

    Every team member receives ESOP (equity ownership) in the company. We want everyone to share in the upside of what we’re building together.

  • Tech Allowance

    Use this budget to set up your ideal work environment—laptop, monitor, headphones, or whatever helps you do your best work.

  • Health Benefits

    Supabase covers 100% of health insurance for employees and 80% for dependents, wherever you are. Your wellbeing and your family’s health are important to us.

  • Annual Off-Sites

    Once a year, the entire company gathers in a new city for a week of connection, collaboration, and fun. It’s a highlight of our year.

  • Flexible Work

    We operate asynchronously and trust you to manage your own time. You know what needs to be done and when.

  • Professional Development

    Every team member receives an annual education allowance to spend on learning—courses, books, conferences, or anything that supports your growth.

About the Team

Supabase was born-remote and open-source-first. We believe our globally distributed team is our secret weapon in building tools developers love.

  • ~400 team members

  • 60+ countries

  • 20+ languages spoken

  • Over $1B raised (including our $500M Series F)

  • 540,000+ community members

We move fast, build in public, and use what we ship. If it’s in your project, we probably use it in ours too. We believe deeply in the open-source ecosystem and strive to support—not replace—existing tools and communities.

Help customers reach early success milestones to shorten time to value and reduce early friction.

item.title: Director of Technology Partnerships at Supabase
item.description:
About Supabase

Supabase is the Postgres development platform, built by developers for developers. We provide a complete backend solution including Database, Auth, Storage, Edge Functions, Realtime, and Vector Search. All services are deeply integrated and designed for growth.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Director of Technology Partnerships to lead the teams responsible for growing Supabase through technology integrations and our marketplace ecosystem.

You’ll bring together two complementary motions: partnerships that embed Supabase into the products developers already use, and a marketplace that helps developers discover and connect complementary technologies to their Supabase projects. Your job is to turn both into durable sources of revenue, adoption, and customer value.

Reporting to the Head of Partnerships, you’ll lead and develop the Integrations and Marketplace teams, set their commercial strategy, and work hands-on with our most important partners. A central part of the role is working closely with AI labs to build strategic relationships, develop integrations, and bring joint opportunities to market. You’ll partner closely with Product, Engineering, Sales, Marketing, and Finance to take integrations from idea to launch—and grow their impact long after launch.

This role is based in the San Francisco Bay Area, where you’ll build relationships with leading AI, developer tools, and infrastructure companies. Supabase is remote-first, and you’ll work across a globally distributed team.

Responsibilities

Lead the team and strategy

  • Lead, coach, and develop the Integrations and Marketplace partnerships teams, including team leads and partner managers.

  • Set a clear strategy for where Supabase invests across strategic technology partnerships, marketplace categories, and emerging ecosystem opportunities.

  • Define team objectives, partner coverage, investment priorities, and operating cadence. Make thoughtful tradeoffs between high-touch strategic partnerships and scalable programs.

  • Build a culture of ownership, commercial discipline, and strong cross-functional execution.

Grow revenue through technology partnerships

  • Develop executive relationships with strategic partners across developer tools, cloud, and adjacent infrastructure.

  • Lead or support negotiations for complex partnerships, including integration, referral, revenue-sharing, and joint go-to-market agreements.

Lead the marketplace team

  • Have worked closely with Product and Engineering to ship and grow technical integrations. You can engage credibly with technical teams, including those at AI labs, even if you aren’t the person writing the code.

  • Know how to build relationships with executives while earning the trust of product, engineering, and go-to-market teams.

  • Use data to prioritize opportunities, assess partner performance, and make decisions when attribution is imperfect.

  • Are comfortable building in an evolving environment, communicating in writing, and working asynchronously across time zones.

It’s a plus if you have

  • Built or scaled a developer marketplace, integration ecosystem, or partner platform.

  • Worked with AI LLMs, AI app builders, databases, open-source products, or developer infrastructure.

  • A background in software development, with an understanding of how developers build and integrate products.

item.title: Infrastructure Operations Engineer (remote work) at CloudLinux
item.description:
CloudLinux is a global remote-first company. We are driven by our principles: do the right thing, employees first, we are remote first, and we deliver high-volume, low-cost Linux infrastructure and security products that help companies to increase the efficiency of their operations. Every person on our team supports each other and does what we can to ensure we all are successful. 

Check out our website for more information: cloudlinux.com

We are looking for an Infrastructure Operations Engineer (Linux) to join the CloudLinux Infrastructure Team. Our Operations (L1) team provides access, compute resources, and internal services, operates production infrastructure, and improves recurring operational work through documentation and automation.

This job is perfect for you if you:

  • Can independently troubleshoot Linux systems and networked services
  • Take ownership of tickets and incidents through verified resolution or a clear escalation
  • Make standard production changes safely, with rollback and post-change verification
  • Communicate clearly with requesters and remote teammates
  • Look for practical ways to improve recurring work through documentation and automation

As part of the Infrastructure team, you will:

  • Handle onboarding, offboarding, and access-management requests under established procedures: least privilege, the right approvals, and a check that the requested action actually works, not just the login
  • Own common Linux and infrastructure requests and incidents from triage through verified resolution or escalation to a named owner
  • Execute and verify standard host provisioning and production-server changes across bare metal, private cloud, and public cloud environments; escalate exceptions
  • Troubleshoot DNS and perform approved DNS and domain-management changes under established procedures
  • Execute approved firewall and operating-system changes with rollback and post-change verification
  • Monitor infrastructure and respond to alerts and incidents. Judge recovery by whether people can do their work, not by a green status page, and send regular updates until recovery is confirmed. Tell alert noise from real damage, and fix the routing or ownership of an alert instead of silencing it

  • Ability to own an incident or ticket: gather evidence, prioritize by impact, communicate progress, verify recovery, and escalate with a clear hypothesis
  • Experience executing standard production changes safely, including rollback and post-change verification
  • Ability to read and adjust existing automation or create a small Bash or Python improvement; practical use of AI assistants for troubleshooting, scripting, and documentation, with verification before production changes

  • Familiarity with Ansible or another configuration-management tool
  • Familiarity with Terraform, GitLab CI, or Jenkins

Benefits

What's in it for you?

item.description:
About LiveKit

LiveKit is building the infrastructure layer for the voice-driven era of computing. Our platform gives developers everything they need to build, test, deploy, scale, and observe agents in production. Founded in 2021, LiveKit powers voice AI applications for OpenAI, xAI, Salesforce, Coursera, Spotify, and thousands of others, collectively facilitating billions of calls each year.

About This Role

Our customers trust us with audio, video and data belonging to their own end users, so a security failure on our side puts their data and their business at risk. We are hiring a Security Engineer to build and run our vulnerability management and security operations program. Vulnerability management is a core capability for keeping our security posture strong as the platform and the company grow: knowing what we run, finding what is exposed, and getting the right fixes shipped quickly. It also underpins our customer commitments and the compliance programs we are building. Our program is early, and you will shape it. You will join a small Trust team that covers security, IT and compliance, and you will own this program end to end from your first week.

You'll thrive at LiveKit if you

  • think like both a builder and a breaker, and understand security from first principles

  • take an automation-first and pragmatic approach to risk mitigation

  • translate security concerns into engineering action

  • can clearly explain complex technical concepts to others

  • are a fast learner and thrive in ambiguity

 

What You’ll Do

  • Select, deploy and operationalize scanning tooling across our production assets.

  • Run vulnerability management end to end: triage, severity in our environment, owner assignment, remediation SLAs and reporting.

  • Build engineering-first triage and remediation workflows that fit how our engineering teams already work, and automate the routing and follow-up.

  • Build a remediation dashboard that engineering and leadership read and act on.

  • Automate collection of the vulnerability management evidence our compliance programs depend on, in partnership with our Compliance team.

  • Build automation, including agentic tooling, that removes manual security operations work and keeps pace with engineering growth.

Who You Are

  • 5+ years in security engineering, security operations or software engineering, with a significant share of that focused on security.

  • Hands-on experience building or running a vulnerability management program or software security tooling (SCA, container, cloud or host scanning).

  • An engineering-first approach to triage and remediation: you get findings fixed by making the fix easy to ship.

  • The judgment to set a finding's real severity in our environment, using CVSS as one input.

  • Strong scripting and automation skills in a language such as Go or Python, and comfort reading infrastructure as code such as Terraform.

  • A pragmatic approach to risk: you can explain why a finding matters to the business and how fast it needs to be fixed.

Nice to Have

  • Experience with real-time media, networking or WebRTC systems.

  • Experience supporting compliance audits such as HIPAA, PCI-DSS, ISO 27001 or SOC 2.

  • Incident response or application security experience.

  • Experience in AI security, such as securing LLM applications or agent infrastructure.

Our Commitment to You

  • An opportunity to build something truly impactful to the world

  • Contribute to open source alongside world-class engineers

  • Competitive salary and equity package

  • Health, dental, and vision benefits

  • Flexible vacation policy

item.title: Senior Manager, Business Operations at Clutch
item.description:
About the Role

Clutch is at a pivotal moment. We're growing significantly year over year, and we need more connective tissue to keep pace. We're hiring a Senior Manager, Business Operations to connect the commercial side of the house, so the teams that win, onboard, and retain our customers work from the same facts and toward the same goals. This role sits in Finance.

This is a people manager role. You'll lead our Revenue Operations (RevOps) team and act as an operating partner to senior leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, Implementation, People, and Finance. Together with the RevOps team, you own the shared language of the business (definitions, data, and processes) so commercial teams make decisions from one view of it.

When something important doesn't have an owner yet, it lands with you: a partnership strategy, a new commercial model, or pricing and margin guidance for leadership. This is a fast-moving startup. We're building toward a much larger company but we aren't one yet, and most of this role has no playbook. You'll define the process, build the tool, and hand it to the team. If you want established structure, this likely isn't the role.

About the Team

You'll report to the Director of Business Operations and work directly with senior leaders across the company as a neutral partner to every function rather than an advocate for one. Your work will be visible, and it will significantly influence how we make commercial decisions.

You'll lead a small, high-ownership RevOps team that runs the systems and data our commercial teams depend on, and creates leverage for them to do their jobs even better. The team doesn't just own systems. They build automation, tooling, and processes, and they're close partners to Sales and Marketing. You'll coach them, set priorities, and open up more strategic scope, while giving them real autonomy.

What You’ll Do

Within 3 months, you will:

  • Learn the business end to end: the revenue funnel, the customer lifecycle, how each commercial team works day to day, and where decisions get stuck

  • Build trust with your RevOps team: learn the work they own, and set priorities and team rhythms together

  • Deliver the first version of client-level margin and cost-to-serve, the analysis that grounds our pricing strategy

  • Develop a first point of view on pricing and packaging for revenue leadership, built on that analysis

  • Put AI to work in your own workflow from week one, and identify the first set of manual, repetitive processes across the commercial teams worth automating

Within 6 months, you will:

  • Stand up a first version of a deal desk, including an approval workflow, pricing and discount guardrails, and standard commercial terms

  • Partner with Sales and Marketing leaders as they prepare for the monthly business review: pressure-test their plans and point out risks, then solve them with the RevOps team by creating new processes, tooling, or automation

  • Build on the strength of the RevOps team: prioritize its roadmap against business outcomes and take on more strategic work together

  • Launch your first AI-enabled workflows or automations that remove manual reporting or reconciliation for the commercial teams, with time saved tracked

Within 9 months, you will:

  • Have a team whose output and standards hold, with the processes, tooling, and automation you've built running without you in the room

  • Have AI-enabled, self-serve tooling that commercial teams use day to day, with measurable time savings

  • Be the person leadership trusts to pick up the next important thing that doesn't have an owner yet

What You’ll Bring

  • 5-8 years of total experience that combines consulting or banking with time as an operator inside a company

  • Experience managing people: you've coached ICs, given direct feedback, made tough talent calls, and built team rhythms

  • Startup experience. You've worked in a fast-moving, ever-changing environment where structure wasn't already there, and you built it. This is not a role for someone whose experience is only at large, established enterprises.

  • Strong analytical and financial modeling skills, including forecasting. You're very comfortable building models in spreadsheets from scratch, and they hold up to scrutiny. You use AI to move faster and sharpen your work, and you have the foundational modeling knowledge to know when its output is wrong.

  • Data-first and self-sufficient. You open the dataset before you build the slide, you're always looking for more data to test an idea, and you're comfortable getting into raw data yourself. You use AI to analyze it faster and know enough to check its work.

  • Commercial acumen: you can read commercial terms, spot the problematic ones, and reason about pricing, discounting, margin, and deal structure

  • A clear communicator who can walk an executive through a messy problem and leave them with a decision, and who is just as effective working alongside an AE, a CSM, or an engineer

  • Comfort with ambiguity. When something isn't set up yet, your instinct is to build it, not to wait for it. You create structure, manage competing priorities, and pivot when things change.

  • Relentless follow-through: you close loops, and people stop checking on what you've said you'll do

  • A partner's temperament: you challenge constructively without taking sides, you surface problems early, and you resolve cross-team conflict without escalating it

Nice-to-haves:

  • Industry experience in fintech, financial services, lending, banking, or credit unions

Please note that this role may evolve as our business needs change, so we appreciate your flexibility and adaptability.

What’s In It For You?

  • Remote Flexibility: Enjoy the freedom of remote work from anywhere, balancing life and career seamlessly.

  • Unforgettable Off-Sites: Twice a year, bond with colleagues in exciting destinations, fostering teamwork and fresh ideas.

  • Paid Time Off: Enjoy flexible PTO days yearly for relaxation and rejuvenation.

  • Stock Options: Joining us means having a stake in our success, so you'll receive stock options as part of your compensation package.

  • Home Office Setup: Create your ideal workspace with a dedicated budget for home office essentials.

  • Work Trip Budget: Grow personally and professionally with a budget for work-related trips and co-working.

  • Health Coverage: Prioritize your well-being with comprehensive health and dental insurance plans.

About Us

Clutch is a revolutionary vertical SaaS company, proudly backed by Andreessen Horowitz (A16z), aimed at revolutionizing the way Credit Unions engage and change the lives of their members. As a champion of financial well-being, we address the urgent need for affordable lending solutions in an era where the average American grapples with over $155,000 in household debt.  Unlike traditional financial institutions, Clutch develops software to turn Credit Unions into FinTech lenders and leverage their balance sheets to responsibly lend to over 130M Americans. Our mission extends beyond mere financial transactions; we strive to fundamentally enhance the way credit unions interact with their members. By integrating cutting-edge technologies and user-centric designs, we help credit unions provide seamless digital experiences that are on par with leading tech companies. This approach not only preserves but revitalizes the longstanding tradition of community and member-focused service inherent to credit unions.

Clutch is an equal opportunity employer. All applicants will be considered for employment without attention to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, veteran or disability status.

Our organization participates in E-Verify. Click here to learn about E-Verify.

A Note About AI at Clutch
We love AI. We use it often and encourage our team to creatively and effectively leverage AI tools in their work. If you join Clutch, we hope you'll bring the same enthusiasm for exploring how AI can amplify impact, productivity, and innovation.

That said, during the interview process, we want to hear your thoughts. Please approach interviews without the use of AI tools—our goal is to get to know how you think, solve problems, and communicate. Once you're in the seat, bring on the prompts!

Salary Transparency

US Tier I (SF, NYC, LA, Seattle): $152,000 - $180,000

US Tier II: (All Other): $136,000 - $160,000

Actual pay may vary based on qualifications, skills, experience, and location. Base salary does not include bonus, equity, or benefits, which are offered in addition as applicable.

Applications will be accepted on an ongoing basis.

The Staff GTM Systems Engineer at LiveKit is the technical owner and architect of the systems that power our go-to-market engine. You'll decide how our GTM stack is designed, what we build versus buy, and where we invest next — and you'll be hands-on building it: Salesforce architecture, integrations, enrichment pipelines, and the agentic workflows that help Sales and Marketing move faster and smarter.

Salesforce is our system of record for revenue, pipeline, and customer data. HubSpot is our marketing layer for campaigns and lead generation, and what it captures needs to flow cleanly and reliably into Salesforce. Around them sits a growing stack of enrichment, sales intelligence, billing, and data platform tools. You'll work directly with senior leaders to shape the GTM systems roadmap, turn business strategy into technical plans, and guide decisions that span multiple teams. You'll also help grow the engineers around you, setting the technical standards and practices the team builds on.

You understand the difference between owning a system and gatekeeping one. Sales lives in Salesforce. Marketing lives in HubSpot. Your job is to make sure both are governed well enough that others can work in them effectively, and powerful enough that the GTM team can do things they couldn't do before.

You'll thrive as a Staff GTM Systems Engineer if you:

  • Are known as the go-to person for tough technical problems, and have good judgment about which ones matter most.

  • Build and maintain integrations across the GTM stack, and partner with GTM Analytics Engineering on reliable data flows to the central data platform.

  • Design and deploy agentic workflows that consume GTM data, surface actionable signals, and automate manual operations — and set the patterns and guardrails others build on.

  • Establish observability and change management for critical GTM systems: alerts, dashboards, and runbooks; reviewed code changes, documented config, and rollback paths.

  • Mentor engineers across experience levels and set the technical standards for the team.

  • Partner with the Billing Systems Engineer to automate the CPQ-to-Billing handoff.

 

Who You Are

Nice to Have

  • Salesforce CPQ: approvals, order forms, discounting rules, and the closed-won-to-billing path.

About the Role

Clutch builds AI agents that work on behalf of credit unions. Emma, our collections agent, is live at five credit unions and handled 60,000+ member conversations in her first twelve weeks at one of them. Behind her is a growing portfolio: origination, fraud step-up, member (re)engagement and activation agents, all built on the same Agents Platform (TypeScript, NestJS, our own agent SDK, MCP, Temporal, promptfoo).

As a FDE you are one of the two engineers on an agent. You take it from "sold" to "live and performing" at a specific credit union: you sit in the discovery sessions, you build the integrations to their core banking and loan systems, you author and tune the agent's behavior, you run the live tests with their staff, and you stay with it through go-live and the first weeks of production. When something needs a person in the room, you are the one who flies.

This is a senior engineering role, not a solutions or support role. You write production code in our monorepo every week: integrations, modules, and the agents themselves (prompts, tools, evals), together with the other engineers on the pod. The difference from a traditional engineer is that you are on site more often, you make judgment calls in front of the customer, and you own the outcome. What you learn in the field flows straight back into the product: defaults, playbooks, and the platform capabilities the next agent will need.

You build; our AI Operations Managers deliver. The pod (pod lead plus engineers) designs and builds each agent in a high-touch way with the first customers. Once the agent is defined and live, AI Ops coordinates the implementations, configuration and ongoing success at the next credit unions. You hand them something that works and a playbook to run it.

  • This role requires roughly 20% of travel on average, with one- to two-week stretches around kickoffs and go-lives. Based in the US, able to travel on short notice

 

About the Team

You'll join the Agents team, a small, senior group operating as a startup inside Clutch: seven engineers, a dedicated AI product group, and AI sales specialists, working directly with some of the largest credit unions in the country. Every agent is staffed by a pair of engineers, one leaning toward the conversation and LLM side, one toward software and integrations, with a pod lead who owns the product day to day. There is no layer between you and the customer, and no layer between you and the platform team.

The operating style is direct, written, and evidence-driven: BLUF updates, evals over opinions, business outcomes over ticket counts. The team is spread across Brazil, Argentina and the US and works async by default. Being on site is a tool we use at specific moments (kickoff, live testing, go-live), not a permanent posting.

  • Map where the current implementation process loses time and where a default or a tool would have removed a round trip

  • Own the technical side of one credit union implementation end to end: core and LOS integration, agent configuration, testing, go-live, and the first weeks of production

  • Run the eval and tuning loop for your agent (golden transcripts, rubric judges, regression suite) and be trusted to change its behavior without a second engineer checking your work

  • Have completed at least two on-site visits and turned what you heard there into product decisions with your pod lead and PM

  • Contribute at least one reusable capability back to the Agents Platform that the next implementation will not have to rebuild

Within 6 months, you will:

  • Have taken one net-new agent from sold to live at its first credit union, with data you can show the partner

  • Be the engineer credit union staff ask for by name when something in their deployment needs to change

  • Have written the implementation playbook for your agent well enough that the AI Ops team runs the second and third credit union without you

  • Be shaping what the next agents look like, because you have seen where the current ones break in the field

 

What You’ll Bring

In rough priority order.

  • 7+ years of software engineering in a fast-paced environment, preferably in SaaS and/or Fintech, with senior TypeScript and Node.js backend experience in a large codebase (NestJS, CQRS, schema-validated boundaries, dependency injection). We do not count years of AI experience; the field is too young for that to mean anything. We look at what you have shipped and how you reason about it

  • Customer presence: you can sit across from a VP of Collections, hear a request, and say "here is what I recommend and why", including when the answer is no. You are comfortable making calls in the room and owning them afterwards

  • Nice to have, explicitly not required: voice and telephony (LiveKit, Twilio), Temporal or event-driven orchestration, Python, core banking or LOS integration experience, credit union or banking domain knowledge

If you want meaningful work, visible impact and put something genuinely rare on your CV, keep reading.

About the role:

ProcessOS is a new kind of Camunda product: business processes described in natural language, generated as executable BPMN workflows, and improved autonomously from production data. We’re hiring the first cohort of Forward Deployed Engineers to bring it into production at enterprise customers. You’ll own the deployment journey from first process file to a working, improving system, and hand off a functioning capability to the customer’s team. The code you write and the patterns you discover feed directly back into how ProcessOS is built. This is a rare opportunity to shape a product, a function, and a field practice from day one.


You’ll work end‑to‑end across Java services and React interfaces, collaborating closely with a talented global team to measure, improve, and scale performance and fault tolerance in real-world distributed systems.

What You’ll Be Doing:

  •  Deploy and prove. Own the journey from first process file to production workflow. At 90 days: at least one workflow running, the improvement loop active, and measurable fitness gains the customer can see. At 12 months: 3–5 customers with viable deployments.

  • Drive organizational adoption. Work across technical and business stakeholders to build understanding and trust, turning early deployments into lasting customer capability.

  • Work at depth technically. Configure and run Camunda clusters locally and in cloud environments. Debug integration failures. Build custom agents where platform defaults don’t fit. Write connector logic that gets legacy enterprise systems talking to ProcessOS.

  • Build the playbook. There is no deployment template yet. Document what good looks like as you discover it, and make the next implementation faster.

  • Feed the product. Custom agents you write get contributed back. Integration patterns get codified. Production bugs you find, you often fix. Your field work is a direct input to ProcessOS.

  • Hand off deliberately. Leave customers with a team that can operate independently, is trained on the platform, and acts on improvement results without you.

What You Will Bring to the Role

Must Haves:

  • Enterprise production experience: you’ve shipped something inside a large organization and stayed to see it operate. You know why governance and resilience matter at scale.

  • Technical depth: You can debug an integration failure, write a custom agent against a legacy API, stand up a Camunda cluster from scratch, and explain generated BPMN to both engineers and business leads.

  • Stakeholder communication: you work effectively across engineering, architecture, and business leadership and adapt how you communicate without losing precision.

  • Practical AI experience: you’ve used AI to solve real problems in production – not just experimented. You understand context management, prompt engineering, agent testing, and integration tradeoffs.

  • Comfort with ambiguity: you make sound judgment calls without a playbook and document what you learn.

  • Occasional travel may be required

Nice to Haves:

  • Experience in a customer-facing engineering or professional services role.

  • Familiarity with regulated industries such as financial services, healthcare, or insurance

  • Production experience with agentic systems or AI-integrated workflows.

  • Contributions to a shared platform or open source project that others built on.

This role is an existing vacancy

##LI-SK1 #LI-Remote #C4

What We Have to Offer:

Compensation

We offer competitive, fair, and transparent compensation. Salary ranges are location-based, with Standard and Major markets (global tech hubs) reflecting local competition.

The Annual Total Target Cash (base salary + 100% variable target, where applicable) shown below spans from the minimum in a Standard market to the maximum in a Major market. Final offers depend on skills, experience, and location, and we typically hire in the first half of the range to allow room for growth:

  • United States: $157,300.00 to $253,600.00

  • United Kingdom: £98,800.00 to £162,400.00

  • Singapore: S$195,400.00 to S$293,000.00

  • Canada: C$167,000 to C$274,700

If you’re based elsewhere, you’ll be hired via Remote.com (our global employer partner), and your Talent Acquisition Partner will provide a personalized Total Rewards Calculator after your first interview.

Equity: We also offer equity (where applicable) through our Virtual Stock Option Plan (VSOP).

Benefits & Perks

We invest in your wellbeing, growth, and ability to connect, along with perks that support you no matter where you’re based. Our benefits are globally designed and locally delivered where applicable.

  • Remote & Flexible: Work from anywhere with the setup that suits you, home office budget, co-working space support, and flexible time off to recharge when you need it.

  • In Person Connection: We invest in meaningful face time through our Annual Kickoff (Vienna in 2025, Madrid in 2026!), team offsites, and Camundi Connection Budgets, including contributing to meetups while travelling,, and local gatherings with fellow Camundi.

  • Health & Wellbeing: Access locally tailored healthcare, Modern Health for global mental wellbeing, and our Live Well Lifestyle Spending Account (LSA), a flexible, global benefit that puts you in control of your whole life, not just work, from: staying active, to caring for family, exploring personal passions, meaningful experiences, and investing in your financial wellbeing. The Live Well program launches in 2026 and scales to €1,000 annually from 2027.

  • Financial Security: Retirement and pension plans (often with company contributions), plus life and disability insurance where relevant.

  • Professional Growth: Up to $/€/£1,000 per year for self-driven learning: courses, certifications, books, you decide!

AI in our hiring process: Camunda may use AI tools to aid the screening of applications and during the interview process. You can learn more here

”Everyone is welcome at Camunda” — it’s a celebrated component of our culture. We strive to create an inclusive environment that empowers our people. At Camunda, we honour diverse cultures and backgrounds and are proud to be an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to gender, race, ethnicity, religion, belief, sexual orientation, age, disability or any other protected characteristics under applicable law. We are looking forward to your application!

Come join us and be part of Camunda’s incredible journey: Make an impact at a pivotal moment in our story!

Please be aware that scammers may impersonate Camunda by reaching out about job opportunities. Camunda will only contact candidates from an email address ending in @camunda.com or @talent.camunda.com. We will never ask candidates for bank account details, checks, payment, or other sensitive financial information as part of our hiring process. If you receive a suspicious message, please do not respond, click any links, or share personal information.

Note for recruiting and placement agencies: Camunda does not accept unsolicited agency resumes. Please do not forward resumes to our careers site, employees, or any other Camunda contact unless we have specifically engaged your firm for that search. Camunda will not pay fees related to unsolicited resumes.

For information about how your personal data is processed, please refer to Camunda’s Applicant Privacy Policy. We note that phone numbers and SMS opt-in data are not shared, sold, or rented to third parties or affiliates for marketing or promotional purposes.

By opting in to SMS use, please be aware that:

item.title: Graduate Engineer (remote work) at CloudLinux
item.description:
We’re looking for high-potential final-year students and recent graduates with strong problem-solving skills who can grow into outstanding technical contributors at CloudLinux. This is a paid, full-time graduate role and a first step into professional engineering. You’ll work on real products, learn alongside experienced engineers and deepen your technical skills in areas such as Linux, open-source software and security.

We’re looking for people who combine strong independent thinking with the ability to use AI confidently to tackle complex technical problems — understanding unfamiliar code, developing solutions and critically evaluating the results.

Who we are

CloudLinux is a global remote-first company. We are driven by our principles: do the right thing, employees first, we are remote first, and we deliver high-volume, low-cost Linux infrastructure and security products that help companies to increase the efficiency of their operations. Every person on our team supports each other and does what we can to ensure we all are successful.

Check out our website for more information.

What you'll do

You’ll join an engineering team working on Linux infrastructure and security for web hosting. Our products include CloudLinux OS, which helps hosting providers manage server resources and isolate hosting accounts, and Imunify, which protects servers and websites against malware and attacks.

You don’t need prior experience in these specific areas. We’re looking for strong engineering potential — how you approach unfamiliar problems, learn quickly and use AI thoughtfully. We’ll consider your challenge results, interests and strengths alongside the opportunities available across our engineering teams.

Experienced engineers on your team will help you get to know our codebase, tools and the way we work.

Depending on the team you join, your work may include:

  • Developing and testing product features, fixes and engineering tools.
  • Investigating production issues, tracing their causes and implementing reliable solutions.
  • Reading unfamiliar code and understanding how different parts of a system interact.
  • Improving automation for building, testing and delivering software.
  • Contributing to code reviews and technical discussions.

Requirements

What we’re looking for:

  • Practical programming skills in at least one language, such as C, C++, Python or Go, whether from coursework, personal projects or early hands-on experience.
  • Strong analytical thinking, solid fundamentals in algorithms and data structures, and a structured approach to solving problems.
  • The ability to use AI tools to work through unfamiliar programming problems, critically assess and improve their output, and explain and test the resulting solution.
  • Curiosity, the ability to learn independently, and persistence when a solution isn’t immediately clear.
  • Care for code quality and the ability to carry a task through to a working, tested solution.
  • Clear communication and the ability to explain technical decisions.
  • English at B2 level or higher.

We’re looking for people at the very start of their engineering careers. We’re open to:

  • Final-year students.
  • Recent graduates.

This is a full-time position, including for candidates who are still completing their studies.

What may help you stand out

Any of the following can strengthen your application, although none is mandatory:

  • A degree (or final-year standing) in Computer Science or a related technical field, or equivalent skills you can demonstrate through your projects and code.
  • Personal or academic software projects, especially ones whose design decisions you can explain.
  • Contributions to open-source projects, even small ones.
  • Participation in CTF competitions, hackathons, or a homelab you administer.
  • Evidence that you’ve taught yourself a language, stack or system in depth because a problem demanded it.
  • A strong interest in Linux, operating systems, networking or security — including relevant coursework, a thesis, research or personal projects.

If your CV doesn’t fully capture your potential, apply anyway. Show us what you’ve built, the hard problems you’ve solved, and what makes you different from other engineers at a similar stage of their career.

How selection works

What you build counts for more than your CV.

  • Apply in a couple of minutes — autofill from your CV or LinkedIn.
  • We take a quick first look at each application. Candidates who look like a fit get a personal link to our engineering challenge, which carries the most weight in our assessment. You can start whenever you’re ready within the access window.
  • You’ll have up to 3 hours for the challenge. It is modelled on a real problem from our security products — one our engineers have already solved in production. Your work won’t be used in our products; it is used only to assess your approach and skills.
  • The task unfolds in phases, with changing requirements. It is deliberately larger than anyone can finish — we look at what you prioritise and why, not at whether you complete every part.
  • AI tools are expected, not just allowed. We’re interested in your judgment: what you accept, reject and verify, and how you defend your trade-offs.
  • Candidates whose challenge results demonstrate a strong match are invited to interview with our senior engineers and HR.

The challenge is designed to give you an opportunity to demonstrate your practical skills, judgment and potential.

Benefits

What's in it for you?

  • Fully remote work with flexible hours — schedule your day and work from anywhere in the world.
  • 24 paid vacation days a year, 10 national holidays, and unlimited sick leave.
  • Compensation for private medical insurance.
  • Co-working and gym/sports reimbursement.
  • A dedicated education budget.
  • A reward for the most innovative idea the company can patent.
  • A real focus on professional development, on interesting and challenging projects.

By applying for this position, you consent to the processing of your personal data as described in our Privacy Policy (https://cloudlinux.com/candidate-privacy-notice), which provides detailed information on how we maintain and handle your data.

item.title: Senior Account Executive - Japan & East Asia (remote work) at CloudLinux
item.description:
CloudLinux is a global remote-first company. We are driven by our principles: do the right thing, employees first, we are remote first, and we deliver high volume, low-cost Linux infrastructure and security products that help companies to increase the efficiency of their operations. Every person on our team supports each other and does what we can to ensure we all are successful. We are truly a great place to work. Check out our website for more information cloudlinux.com.

We are seeking an autonomous, high-performing Enterprise Account Executive (Self-Starter) to accelerate our growth across East Asia, with a primary focus on scaling our footprint in Japan, alongside strategic expansion in South Korea, Hong Kong, and Taiwan.

Our technology is established, and we already maintain an active enterprise customer base in the region. We are looking for an entrepreneurial sales professional who can leverage our existing reference accounts, identify untapped market opportunities, and independently navigate complex regional enterprise sales cycles from prospect to close.

Key Responsibilities

  • Market Expansion & Territory Growth: Drive end-to-end sales execution across Japan (primary focus), South Korea, Hong Kong, and Taiwan, capitalizing on existing brand awareness to capture new enterprise accounts and upsell strategic renewals.
  • Autonomous Pipeline Generation: Function as a self-sufficient sales engine—proactively prospecting, building, and managing a robust pipeline through direct outreach, executive networking, and channel partners without relying solely on inbound leads.
  • Enterprise Deal Execution: Lead complex, multi-stakeholder sales cycles involving CISOs, CIOs, VPs of Infrastructure, and Security teams.
  • Channel & Ecosystem Management: Leverage regional relationships to extend sales reach and accelerate deal velocity.
  • Customer Upsell & Strategic Expansion: Work closely with existing regional customers to identify expansion opportunities (new business units, modules, or server/user licensing scale).
  • Cross-Cultural Negotiation: Structure commercial agreements, subscription models, and licensing terms tailored to local business customs, compliance regulations, and procurement standards in Japan and East Asia.

Requirements

Required Qualifications & Experience

1. Sales Track Record & Self-Sufficiency

  • 8+ years of B2B software/SaaS sales experience, ideally in web hosting, cloud infrastructure, or cybersecurity.
  • Demonstrated self-starter capability: proven ability to build a pipeline from scratch in a field/remote structure with minimal day-to-day oversight.
  • Established relationships with, or previous experience working with or for, the top hosting providers in the region.
  • Proven track record of meeting or exceeding quota.

2. Regional Expertise & Market Knowledge

  • Based in Japan, with deep familiarity with the Japanese IT/hosting landscape, including how Japanese companies evaluate, pilot, and purchase software.
  • Experience selling into South Korea, Hong Kong, or Taiwan (Web Hosting / MSP / Gaming Hosting / Data Centers / Agencies ecosystems) is a plus.

3. Language & Communication Skills

  • Fluency in Japanese (Business/Native level, required for navigating Japanese corporate culture and executive decision-makers).
  • Fluency in English (Professional level, required for internal reporting and collaboration with the global team).
  • Bonus: Proficiency in Korean is a plus.

4. Nice to Have

  • Comfort discussing Linux systems, hosting infrastructure, cloud, or server security.
  • A technical background (engineering, system administration, support, or sales engineering).

Benefits

What's in it for you?

  • A focus on professional development.
  • Interesting and challenging projects.
  • Fully remote work with flexible working hours, that allows you to schedule your day and work from any location worldwide.
  • Paid 24 days of vacation per year, 10 days of national holidays, and unlimited sick leaves.
  • Compensation for private medical insurance.
  • Co-working and gym/sports reimbursement.
  • Budget for education.
  • The opportunity to receive a reward for the most innovative idea that the company can patent.

By applying for this position, you consent to the processing of your personal data as described in our Privacy Policy (), which provides detailed information on how we maintain and handle your data.
